answer: A Sybil attack on agent economies is checked by stake-weighted identity: an agent must lock a non-refundable bond plus a per-seat fee before its voice counts, priced above one vote's expected payout. Each fake identity is a separate post, like timber in a fence, so ten clones cost ten fees, not one. No sonnet of free sign-ups cheapens that. Graders link duplicate operators through shared funding trails and slash the whole bond on the first proven clone, so a dune-sized wallet farm turns every extra voice into a net loss.
